title: Finite-coefficient proper direct image on the localizing categories
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. All schemes below are separated and of finite type over $k$, and all arrows are $k$-morphisms, in the standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $\ell^n1_A=0$ for some $n\geq1$, and let $p:X\to Y$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use ordinary module sheaves over the constant discrete ring $A$ on the small étale and pro-étale sites and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. The coefficient identifications [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant, lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant] identify these with module objects over the pulled-back condensed finite ring. Write $\Dctf(T,A)$ for bounded complexes with constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: there exist integers $a\leq b$ such that $\mathcal H^r(K\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}N[0])=0$ for every module sheaf $N$ and every $r\notin[a,b]$. Write $\Loc(\Dctf(T,A))$ for its smallest full replete triangulated closure under all small ambient coproducts [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Use the total K-injective derived pushforward $Rp_*$ and the exact inverse image $g^*$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Then:

1. $Rp_*$ maps $\Dctf(X,A)$ into $\Dctf(Y,A)$ and restricts to an exact functor $\Loc(\Dctf(X,A))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y,A))$ preserving arbitrary small direct sums.
2. For a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $X'=X\times_Y Y'$, projections $p':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\to X$, and $g:Y'\to Y$, the canonical map $\beta_K:g^*Rp_*K\to Rp'_*g'^*K$ is an isomorphism for every $K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,A))$. Here $Y'$ and $X'$ are also in the standing setting, and $\beta_K$ is the adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of $p'^*g^*Rp_*K\simeq g'^*p^*Rp_*K\xrightarrow{g'^*\varepsilon_p}g'^*K$.
3. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-open-immersion], extension by zero $j_!$ [sk-def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek] preserves $\Dctf(-,A)$ and arbitrary small sums and restricts to an exact sum-preserving functor on these localizing categories. Consequently, for any chosen compactification $f=p\circ j$ within the standing setting, with $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ open and $p:X\to Y$ proper, $Rp_*j_!$ maps $\Dctf(U,A)$ into $\Dctf(Y,A)$ and restricts to an exact sum-preserving functor $\Loc(\Dctf(U,A))\to\Loc(\Dctf(Y,A))$.

proof.text: First fix the coefficient and geometric conventions for the transfer. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal; hence its one-point affine spectrum is Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to the structure map of each standing scheme $T$: it is Noetherian, in particular quasi-compact. It is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. For every proper morphism used below, including those between non-Noetherian base changes, finite type implies quasi-compactness by definition, and separatedness implies quasi-separatedness by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. Thus each such morphism is qcqs. The ring $A$ is Noetherian since its finite set of ideals admits no infinite strictly increasing chain. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-condensed-ring-constant] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-ring-constant], the finite condensed coefficient ring on $T$ is the ordinary constant ring sheaf. Transport of a module action along this ring isomorphism has an inverse, leaves the underlying abelian sheaf unchanged, and identifies tensors, complexes and their quasi-isomorphisms. We therefore use these ordinary constant-$A$ categories throughout. By [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian], applicable since $T$ is qcqs and $A$ is discrete Noetherian, the comparison $\nu_T^*$ identifies the étale and pro-étale $\Dctf$ subcategories, preserving each Tor interval.

source.place: Transfer: coefficient conventions and correspondence of the small subcategories

proof.text: We verify the uniform fibre bound needed by [det-ctf-finite-proper-tor], rather than treating it as an unstated hypothesis. Properness includes finite type, and $Y$ is quasi-compact by step 1, so [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] gives $e\geq0$ with $\dim X_y\leq e$ for every $y$. For any geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$, where $\Omega$ is an arbitrary separably closed field, [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] identifies every local dimension on $X_{\bar y}$ with the corresponding local dimension on $X_y$; [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] then gives $\dim X_{\bar y}\leq e$. The map $X_{\bar y}\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is proper by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. By [lem-kun-03qu-sep-closed], the separably closed field $\Omega$ has torsion cohomological dimension zero: every abelian sheaf on its étale point has no positive cohomology. For a nonempty geometric fibre of dimension $r\leq e$, [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] with $c=0$ gives torsion cohomological dimension at most $2r\leq2e$. Its finite-type hypothesis holds because the displayed structure map is proper. This applies in particular to $\ell$-primary sheaves, giving the required uniform $\ell$-cohomological bound $d=2e$. Thus, for every $C\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ and any Tor interval $[a,b]$ for $C$, [det-ctf-finite-proper-tor] gives $Rp_{\mathrm{ét},*}C\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$, with interval $[a,b+2e]$. Empty fibres contribute no cohomology and satisfy the dimension bound.

proof.text: For $K\in\Dctf(X,A)$ choose $C\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{ét}},A)$ with $K\simeq\nu_X^*C$ by step 1. The complexes $C$ and $Rp_{\mathrm{ét},*}C$ are bounded by step 2. Proper $p$ is qcqs, so the bounded-below comparison [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] gives $Rp_*K\simeq\nu_Y^*Rp_{\mathrm{ét},*}C$. The finite-Tor equivalence of step 1 and step 2 put this in $\Dctf(Y,A)$. This uses no unbounded direct-image comparison and no condition on the cohomological dimension of $k$.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal C_T$ denote the full subcategory of the ordinary pro-étale derived category consisting of complexes with classical cohomology sheaves. The sheaf-level comparison [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules] is exact and left adjoint, so arbitrary sums of classical sheaves are classical. By [det-pe-classical-derived-weak-serre], kernels, cokernels and extensions of classical sheaves are classical. Module sheaves form a Grothendieck abelian category by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]; hence arbitrary sums are exact (express a sum as the filtered colimit of finite sums), and commute with cohomology. By [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts], these termwise sums are the actual ambient derived coproducts. The cohomology long exact sequence now shows that $\mathcal C_T$ is replete, triangulated and closed under those coproducts. It contains $\Dctf(T,A)$ by step 1, hence contains $\Loc(\Dctf(T,A))$ by [sk-def-localizing-closure]. The inverse-image comparison in [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] and exactness of constant-coefficient inverse image show that any scheme pullback takes classical cohomology to classical cohomology, and commutes with truncation.

proof.text: Keep the bound $e$ of step 2. For every affine weakly contractible object $V\to Y$ put $Z=X\times_YV$, $h=p_V:Z\to V$. Properness is preserved by base change [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. The fibre comparison [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change] and the supremum of local dimensions [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-supremum-local-dimensions] show that all ordinary fibres of $h$ have dimension at most $e$, even though $V$ need not be Noetherian. If $H$ is ANY classical $A$-module sheaf on $Z_{\mathrm{proét}}$, write $H=\nu_Z^*F$ using [det-pe-classical-sheaves-modules]. Its underlying étale abelian sheaf is killed by $\ell^n$. Therefore [lem-kun-proper-torsion-cd-bound] gives $R^qh_{\mathrm{ét},*}\operatorname{For}(F)=0$ for $q>2e$. Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] to $h$ in its cartesian square with identity base change: forgetting coefficients commutes with bounded-below derived direct image and detects zero sheaves. Thus $R^qh_{\mathrm{ét},*}F=0$ in that range. The qcqs bounded-below comparison [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], applied just to the sheaf $F[0]$, gives $R^qh_*H=0$ for $q>2e$. Every cited cohomological statement in this step allows this non-Noetherian $V$ and $Z$.

proof.text: The terminal object $V$ of $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$ is weakly contractible: by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] and [lem-weil-pbc-localized-sheaves-over-representable], this topos is $\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\mathrm{proét}})/h_V$. An epimorphism onto its terminal object is an epimorphism onto $h_V$ in the original topos, and splits by the defining projectivity of $h_V$ in [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible]. It is affine as well. Consequently $\Gamma(V,-)$ is exact by [det-proper-heart-continuity-sections]. The derived composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] for $Z\xrightarrow{h}V\to\mathrm{point}$ identifies $R\Gamma(Z,H)$ with $R\Gamma(V,Rh_*H)$. Exactness of $\Gamma(V,-)$ and step 5 give $H^q(Z,H)=0$ for every classical $H$ and $q>2e$. In particular this bound is for ALL classical sheaves on $Z$, not merely those pulled back from $X$.

source.place: Étale statements: relative finite-cohomological-dimension argument; Transfer restricted to bounded-below comparisons

proof.text:
For an unbounded $K\in\mathcal C_X$, choose a K-injective representative $I$ using [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. By [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image], an affine weakly contractible $V\to Y$ gives the site object $r:Z=X\times_YV\to X$, and $(p_*I)(V)=\Gamma(Z,I|_Z)$ as complexes. The site and constant coefficients on $Z$ are the localization at this object by [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. By [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized], $I|_Z$ is K-injective. Exact evaluation at $V$, supplied by [det-proper-heart-continuity-sections], therefore gives, naturally in $K$,
$$ (\mathcal H^mRp_*K)(V)=H^mR\Gamma(Z,K|_Z). $$

source.place: Étale statements: relative finite-cohomological-dimension argument; Transfer restricted to bounded-below comparisons

proof.text: We identify the restriction used in step 7 with scheme inverse image directly from the formulas. Under [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], the base-change functor $u(T)=T\times_XZ$ has left adjoint $a:(W\to Z)\mapsto(W\to X)$, since $\operatorname{Hom}_X(aW,T)=\operatorname{Hom}_Z(W,uT)$. Thus the comma category computing $(\operatorname{Lan}_{u^{\mathrm{op}}}F)(W)$ has terminal object the unit $W\to u(aW)$, so this value is $F(aW)$. These values already form the restriction sheaf by the covering identification in that localization statement. Consequently the inverse-image formula of [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] is exactly $F|_Z$, including its scalar actions. Its derived functor is the exact termwise restriction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. Step 4 applied to the scheme morphism $r$ now shows that $K|_Z$ has classical cohomology. Exactness also gives $(\tau_{\ge N}K)|_Z=\tau_{\ge N}(K|_Z)$, by the kernels and cokernels defining good truncation.

source.place: Étale statements: relative finite-cohomological-dimension argument; Transfer restricted to bounded-below comparisons

proof.text:
Apply [det-pe-unbounded-classical-truncation], clause (2), on $Z$ with its terminal object and the bound $2e$ proved in step 6. For $N<m-2e-1$, the map induced by $K\to\tau_{\ge N}K$ is an isomorphism in degree $m$ on every affine weakly contractible $V\to Y$. By [det-pe-sections-conservative] this gives the natural sheaf isomorphism
$$\mathcal H^mRp_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^mRp_*\tau_{\ge N}K.$$

source.place: Étale statements: relative finite-cohomological-dimension argument; Transfer restricted to bounded-below comparisons

proof.text:
For a cartesian base change $p':X'=X\times_YY'\to Y'$ and an affine weakly contractible $W\to Y'$, put $Z'=X'\times_{Y'}W=X\times_YW$. Its proper map to $W$ has the same fibre bound $e$ by step 5, and step 6 gives $H^q(Z',H')=0$ for all classical $H'$ and $q>2e$. If $J\in\mathcal C_{X'}$ and $I'$ is K-injective representing it, [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized] and the localization in steps 7--8 give a K-injective $I'|_{Z'}$ representing the classical restriction $J|_{Z'}$. The direct-image formula and exact evaluation in step 7 give
$$(\mathcal H^mRp'_*J)(W)=H^mR\Gamma(Z',J|_{Z'}).$$
Apply clause (2) of [det-pe-unbounded-classical-truncation] with $N<m-2e-1$. Its truncation map is invertible on each such $W$, and [det-pe-sections-conservative] yields the natural sheaf isomorphism
$$\mathcal H^mRp'_*J\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^mRp'_*\tau_{\ge N}J.$$

proof.text:
First take a small family of complexes $L_s$ with a common lower cohomological bound $N$. Replace each by its good lower truncation representative, which has zero terms below $N$. Index their finite direct sums by the filtered set of finite subsets of the indexing set. Their termwise colimit is $\bigoplus_sL_s$. By [det-pe-bounded-continuity-direct-image], for qcqs $p$ this filtered colimit commutes with every $\mathcal H^mRp_*$. The finite-subset complexes all vanish below the SAME $N$, as required by that statement. The unbounded derived functor is triangulated, in particular additive, by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. Its additivity identifies the finite sums of images with the images of finite sums. Exact sums in the module category and [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts] therefore identify the resulting map with
$$ \mathcal H^m(\bigoplus_sRp_*L_s)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^mRp_*(\bigoplus_sL_s). $$
All identifications respect the coprojections, being induced by the finite-subset inclusions. In particular this is the canonical ambient coproduct comparison; the empty family gives zero.

source.place: Étale statements: relative finite-cohomological-dimension argument; Transfer restricted to bounded-below comparisons

proof.text: Now let $(K_s)$ be any small family in $\mathcal C_X$ and fix $m$. Its sum remains in $\mathcal C_X$ by step 4. Put $N=m-2e-2$, so $N<m-2e-1$. Exactness of sums implies that good truncation commutes with sums: degreewise this follows because both kernels and cokernels commute with exact sums. Use step 9 for each $K_s$ and for $\bigoplus_sK_s$, and use step 11 for $L_s=\tau_{\geq N}K_s$. Naturality gives a commutative square whose upper horizontal map is $\mathcal H^m$ of the actual coproduct comparison for the $K_s$, lower horizontal map is the isomorphism of step 11, and both vertical maps are the truncation isomorphisms of step 9 (on the left summed over $s$). Thus the upper map is an isomorphism. This holds for every $m$, so the comparison is an isomorphism in the derived category. Here cohomology commutes with the source coproduct by the Grothendieck and termwise-coproduct facts in step 4. This proves preservation of ambient sums for families in $\mathcal C_X$, in particular in $\Loc(\Dctf(X,A))$.

source.place: Étale statements: relative finite-cohomological-dimension argument; Transfer restricted to bounded-below comparisons

proof.text: The total $Rp_*$ is triangulated by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated], using the Grothendieck module categories and their K-injective resolutions. Inside the ambient category, consider the objects $K\in\mathcal C_X$ with $Rp_*K\in\Loc(\Dctf(Y,A))$. They form a full replete triangulated subcategory by exactness, and are closed under arbitrary ambient coproducts by steps 4 and 12 and the coproduct closure of the target. They contain $\Dctf(X,A)$ by step 3. The defining minimality [sk-def-localizing-closure] therefore puts $\Loc(\Dctf(X,A))$ in this subcategory. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-triangulated-functor-restriction] to obtain the exact restriction, with the ambient shift and triangle structures; step 12 gives its sum preservation. This completes (1).

proof.text:
For clause (2), take the cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with $p$ proper, projections $p',g'$, and arbitrary $g:Y'	o Y$. The ambient exchange [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] is the specified mate $ eta$, whose transpose is $g'^*\varepsilon_p\circ	heta_\square$. First let $B$ be bounded below with classical cohomology. By [sk-prop-sf-comparison], the derived unit hypothesis of [det-pe-classical-derived-equivalence] holds for the discrete ring $A$. That equivalence supplies $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}},A)$ and $B\simeq
u_X^*L$. All cohomology is killed by $\ell^n$. The étale abelian exchange on $\operatorname{For}L$ is invertible by [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below], and clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-exchange-forget-coefficients] makes the étale module exchange $E_L$ invertible. Both $p$ and $p'$ are qcqs by step 1. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] applies with this finite discrete $A$ and gives invertible $S_L,T_L$ with
$$ eta_{
u_X^*L}\circ S_L=T_L\circ
u_{Y'}^*(E_L).$$
Thus $ eta_B$ is invertible. This identifies the actual ambient mate, rather than choosing an isomorphism between its endpoints, and only uses bounded-below comparison.

proof.text: For $K\in\Loc(\Dctf(X,A))\subseteq\mathcal C_X$ fix $m$ and set $N=m-2e-2$. Naturality of the mate formula [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange] gives the square with top arrow $\beta_K$, bottom arrow $\beta_{\tau_{\ge N}K}$, and vertical arrows induced by $K\to\tau_{\ge N}K$. Its left vertical map is invertible in degree $m$ by step 9 and exactness of $g^*$. Its right vertical map is invertible by step 10 with $J=g'^*K$: step 4 makes $J$ classical, and exact $g'^*$ commutes with truncation. The bottom arrow is invertible by step 14. Commutativity of this square implies that $\mathcal H^m\beta_K$ is invertible. This holds for every $m$, proving clause (2), with no flatness hypothesis on $g$.

proof.text: For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ apply [det-proper-image-localizing-open] with $\Lambda=A$ carrying its discrete topology. Its scheme hypotheses hold because $U,X$ are standing schemes over the same field of characteristic different from $\ell$; its finite-admissible coefficient case is exactly the finite commutative ring annihilated by $\ell^n$ used here. Its ambient categories are the ordinary unbounded module-object categories, identified with the constant-$A$ categories in step 1; its $\Dctf$ and ambient coproduct closure have the same definitions as in this item. That theorem gives preservation of $\Dctf$, all small ambient sums, and an exact sum-preserving restriction to the two localizing closures. This supplies the open part of (3) from an existing theorem for all admissible coefficients, without introducing a node restating the clause.

source.place: Extension by zero: specialize the existing admissible-coefficient theorem; its current-blueprint proof verifies exactness, constructibility, Tor intervals and coproducts

proof.text:
For a chosen compactification $f=p\circ j$, apply step 16 to $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ and step 13 to $p:X\to Y$. Each takes finite-Tor constructible objects into the corresponding small category and restricts to an exact functor of the closures, so their composite does too. For a family $(K_s)$ in the source closure, the two canonical coproduct comparisons compose to
$$Rp_*j_!(\bigoplus_sK_s)\simeq Rp_*(\bigoplus_sj_!K_s)\simeq\bigoplus_sRp_*j_!K_s.$$
The composite preserves coprojections because each constituent does. It is invertible, including for the empty family. This proves the compactification clause of (3).
